name: core/notation
title: Notation and traps
summary: Writing proofs the way typeset notes write them, and the mistakes the checker must refuse.

entries.title: Theorem 1.1 in Unicode
entries.source:
Theorem: "Triangle inequality"
Claim: ∀ a ∈ ℝ, ∀ b ∈ ℝ, |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|
Proof:
    Let a, b : ℝ
    Step: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|
QED

entries.title: Definition 2.6 shape: forall eps > 0, exists delta > 0
entries.source:
Theorem: "lim 3x = 6 at x = 2, epsilon-delta"
Claim: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x ∈ ℝ, |x − 2| < δ ⇒ |3·x − 6| < ε
Proof:
    Given ε : ℝ where ε > 0
    Let δ = ε / 3
    Subproof:
        Given x : ℝ
        Assume |x − 2| < δ
        Step: |3·x − 6| = 3·|x − 2|
        Step: < 3·δ
        Step: = ε
    Therefore ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x ∈ ℝ, |x − 2| < δ ⇒ |3·x − 6| < ε [witness: ε / 3]
QED

entries.title: Example 2.20 with ∞ and \infty
entries.source:
Step: lim(1/x, x, 0, "+") = ∞
Step: \lim_{x \to 0^-} 1/x = -\infty
Step: lim(x², x, -∞) = ∞

entries.title: Example 3.22 geometric series in Unicode
entries.source:
Let r ∈ ℝ
Assume |r| < 1
Step: \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^k = 1/(1 − r)

entries.title: |S_n| = n! written with the postfix bang
entries.source:
Let n : ℕ
Assume n ≥ 1
Step: n! = n·(n − 1)!
Step: 5! = 120

entries.title: Remark 4 with superscript inverses
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Given a, b : G
Step: (a·b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹·a⁻¹
Step: a·a⁻¹ = e
Step: a²·a³ = a⁵
Step: a⁰ = e

entries.title: Elements declared with ∈
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Let g ∈ G
Step: g·e = g
Step: e·g = g

entries.title: Bounded quantifier over a group carrier
entries.source:
Theorem: "Every element has an inverse"
Claim: Group(G, op, e, inv) => ∀ a ∈ G, ∃ b ∈ G, op(a, b) = e
Proof:
    Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
    Given a : G
    Therefore exists b : G, op(a, b) = e [witness: inv(a)]
QED

entries.title: Logical connectives in Unicode
entries.source:
Let x : ℝ
Assume h: x > 2 ∧ x < 5
Therefore x > 1 ∨ x < -1
Therefore ¬(x = 0)
Therefore x ≠ 0

entries.title: Greek letters typed directly
entries.source:
Let α, β : ℝ
Assume α < β
Step: (α + β)/2 < β
Step: α < (α + β)/2

entries.title: Sinh, arctan, floor and binomial
entries.source:
Let x : ℝ
Step: cosh(x)^2 - sinh(x)^2 = 1
Step: tan(atan(x)) = x
Step: floor(7/2) = 3
Step: binomial(5, 2) = 10

entries.title: Oo is not a real number
entries.source:
Let a : Real
Step: oo - 1 < oo - 2
entries.explanation: ∞ is not a number you can subtract from: ∞ − 1 and ∞ − 2 are both ∞, so neither is less than the other.

entries.title: -oo is below every real, not above
entries.source:
Let a : Real
Step: -oo > a
entries.explanation: In the extended reals −∞ < a for every real a, so −∞ > a is false.

entries.title: Oo * 0 is indeterminate
entries.source: Step: oo * 0 = 0
entries.explanation: 0 · ∞ is an indeterminate form; the notes leave it undefined.

entries.title: A declared oo is an ordinary variable
entries.source:
Let oo : Real
Step: oo > 5
entries.explanation: Once `oo` is declared as a variable it is just a real number, so nothing makes it greater than 5.

entries.title: Limits at infinity have one side only
entries.source: Step: lim(1/x, x, oo, "+") = 0
entries.explanation: x can only approach ∞ from below, so a direction such as "+" makes no sense there.

entries.title: Sin(1/x) has no limit at 0
entries.source: Step: lim(sin(1/x), x, 0) = 0
entries.explanation: sin(1/x) oscillates between −1 and 1 in every neighbourhood of 0 (Example 2.34), so it has no limit.

entries.title: Geometric series needs |r| < 1
entries.source:
Let r : Real
Step: sum(k, 0, oo, r^k) = 1/(1 - r)
entries.explanation: Σ rᵏ converges to 1/(1 − r) only when |r| < 1; with nothing known about r the sum may diverge.

entries.title: Partial geometric sum needs r != 1
entries.source:
Let r : Real
Let n : Nat
Step: sum(k, 0, n, r^k) = (1 - r^(n + 1))/(1 - r)
entries.explanation: At r = 1 the partial sum is n + 1 and (1 − rⁿ⁺¹)/(1 − r) divides by zero; the closed form needs r ≠ 1.

entries.title: Rho^n -> 0 needs rho < 1
entries.source:
Let \rho : Real
Assume \rho > 1
Step: lim(\rho^n, n, oo) = 0
entries.explanation: For ρ > 1, ρⁿ → ∞ (Example 3.8), not 0.

entries.title: |sin| <= 1 does not give |sin| <= 1/2
entries.source:
Let x : Real
Step: |sin(x)| <= 1/2
entries.explanation: sin reaches 1 (at π/2), so |sin x| ≤ 1/2 is false in general.

entries.title: Exp > 0 does not give exp > 1
entries.source:
Let x : Real
Step: exp(x) > 1
entries.explanation: eˣ < 1 for every x < 0.

entries.title: Log is not bounded below by its argument
entries.source:
Let x : Real
Assume x > 0
Step: log(x) >= x - 1
entries.explanation: log x ≤ x − 1 for x > 0, with equality only at 1; the reverse inequality fails, e.g. at x = 2.

entries.title: Symbolic gcd is not 1
entries.source:
Let n, k : Int
Step: gcd(n, k) = 1
entries.explanation: gcd(n, k) depends on n and k: gcd(4, 6) = 2.

entries.title: Symbolic lcm is not the product
entries.source:
Let n, k : Int
Step: lcm(n, k) = n * k
entries.explanation: lcm(n, k) = nk only when gcd(n, k) = 1: lcm(4, 6) = 12, not 24.

entries.title: Wrong factorial
entries.source: Step: 4! = 12

entries.title: Congruent mod 0 is equality
entries.source:
Let a : Int
Step: a + 1 = a (mod 0)
entries.explanation: Modulo 0, a ≡ b means b − a is a multiple of 0, i.e. a = b; a + 1 ≠ a.

entries.title: Congruence does not survive division
entries.source:
Let i, k, n : Int
Assume h: 2 * i = 2 * k (mod n)
Therefore i = k (mod n)
entries.explanation: 2i ≡ 2k (mod n) does not give i ≡ k (mod n) when n is even: i = 0, k = 2, n = 4.

entries.title: (ab)^-1 is not a^-1 b^-1 in a group
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Given a, b : G
Step: (a * b)^-1 = a^-1 * b^-1
entries.explanation: (ab)⁻¹ = b⁻¹a⁻¹ (Remark 4); a⁻¹b⁻¹ is a different word unless the group is abelian.

entries.title: But (ab)^-1 = a^-1 b^-1 in an abelian group
entries.source:
Assume AbelianGroup(G, op, e, inv)
Given a, b : G
Step: (a * b)^-1 = a^-1 * b^-1

entries.title: A^2 b^2 is not (ab)^2 in a group
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Given a, b : G
Step: a^2 * b^2 = (a * b)^2
entries.explanation: (ab)² = abab, which equals a²b² = aabb only if ba = ab.

entries.title: Real variables still commute under *
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Let x, y : Real
Step: x * y = y * x

entries.title: A hypothesis can make two words equal
entries.source:
Assume Group(G, op, e, inv)
Given a, b : G
Assume h: op(a, b) = op(b, a)
Step: op(op(a, b), inv(a)) = b

entries.title: An undeclared type is still refused
entries.source: Given a : Widget
entries.explanation: Widget is neither a number type nor a structure's carrier, so it cannot be a type.

entries.title: Bounded exists keeps its guard
entries.source:
Let x : Real
Therefore exists d > 0, d < 0
entries.explanation: ∃ d > 0 with d < 0 asks for a number that is both positive and negative.

entries.title: Bounded forall keeps its guard
entries.source: Therefore forall x > 0, x > 1
entries.explanation: ∀ x > 0, x > 1 fails at x = 1/2.

entries.title: A sum that divides by zero is undefined
entries.source: Step: sum(k, -1, 1, 1/k) = 0
entries.explanation: The index runs through k = 0, where 1/k is undefined, so the sum has no value.
